claims.claim: Dasharatha tells the story himself, to Kausalya, at midnight, remembering his old misdeed

shots.hi: दशरथ के बाण से मरे उस बेटे का, वाल्मीकि ने कोई नाम ही नहीं लिखा। तो श्रवण कुमार का नाम, आया कहाँ से, आज यही देखते हैं।
shots.en: Valmiki never wrote a name for the son Dasharatha's arrow killed. So where did the name Shravan Kumar come from? Let's see.

sloka.en: “With one arrow, struck in my vital spot, two are killed with me: my blind, aged mother and father.”
sloka.translit: ekena khalu bāṇena marmaṇyabhihate mayi, dvāvandhau nihatau vṛddhau mātā janayitā ca me

shots.en: In the dark, on the bank of the Sarayu, the prince went out to hunt. A sound came from the water, like a pot being filled. He thought it was an elephant, and shot at the sound.

caption: We all know the story of Shravan Kumar, the son who carried his blind parents on a pilgrimage. In Valmiki's Ramayana (Critical Edition, Ayodhya 2.57-58), King Dasharatha tells the story himself to Kausalya, at midnight, on the night he dies. The young man is never named: Valmiki calls him only "the ascetic" and "the sage's son". There is no pilgrimage and no kavad: he came alone to the Sarayu at night to fetch water for his blind parents. He asked Dasharatha to pull out the arrow and tell his father, and after death he rose to heaven in divine form. Tulsidas too writes only "तापस अंध साप सुधि आई". Both tellings are told with devotion.
